blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At scale, digital productivity is no longer about individual habits. It is about the shape of the whole company's attention. Every company-wide tool rollout, every default setting, every meeting template quietly shapes how people spend their days. A tiny change to a default — notifications turned off by default, meetings capped at fifty minutes, calendars showing 'focus time' blocks — can free enormous amounts of collective energy over a year.

The senior leader's job is to see the defaults and to change them deliberately. Most companies carry default settings that nobody chose; they were simply never revisited after the tool was installed. Choosing them consciously, in the service of how the company wants people to work, is one of the quietest forms of leadership available.

Digital hygiene at scale is not about discipline imposed on individuals. It is about environments that quietly make the right behaviour the easy one. That is a design problem, not a willpower problem.

items.q: According to the text, at scale digital productivity is primarily about…
options: the number of tools a company installs
the shape of the whole company's attention
items.why: "It is about the shape of the whole company's attention" — deixa de ser hábito individual e passa a ser coletivo.

items.q: Why do most companies carry default settings that nobody chose?
options: They were selected by a committee and later reversed
They were designed to reduce collective energy
They were imposed by the software vendor by contract
They were never revisited after the tool was installed
items.why: "they were simply never revisited after the tool was installed."

items.q: What kind of problem does the author say digital hygiene really is?
items.why: "That is a design problem, not a willpower problem."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: The right behaviour should be made the easy one.
Productivity at scale is best fixed by urging staff to be more disciplined.
Defaults quietly shape how people spend their days.
Small changes to defaults can free large amounts of energy.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta contra disciplina imposta ao indivíduo — o remédio é o ambiente, não o sermão.

items.q: Describing consciously chosen defaults as "one of the quietest forms of leadership" suggests that…
options: leaders should avoid changing any settings
quiet leaders are less effective than assertive ones
leadership works best when it is loud and visible
meaningful leadership can be invisible and structural
items.why: Inferência: escolher defaults é discreto, mas molda o trabalho de centenas — liderança real sem estardalhaço.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily explicando a mudança de configurações padrão em toda a empresa. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So this went live on Monday, and I want to be honest about how small it actually is. We changed three defaults. Just three. Notifications are now off by default — people can switch them back on, but almost nobody does. Meetings are capped at fifty minutes instead of an hour, so you get ten minutes to breathe. And everyone's calendar now shows two focus-time blocks a week, already carved out.

Nobody was told to work differently. No memo, no training, no productivity webinar. We simply changed what happens if you do nothing — and it turns out most people do nothing. That's the whole trick.

What I did not expect was how quiet the effect would be. There was no dramatic before-and-after. But look at the numbers across a few hundred people and the after-hours pings are down by a third, and focus blocks are actually being protected. Nobody is celebrating it, because nobody really noticed it happen. And that, honestly, is the point. The environment is doing the work that we used to ask willpower to do.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How many defaults did Emily's team change?
items.why: "We changed three defaults. Just three."

items.q: What now happens to notifications by default?
options: They are turned off, though people may switch them back on
They are grouped into a single daily digest
They are permanently disabled and cannot be restored
They are left exactly as the software installed them
items.why: "Notifications are now off by default — people can switch them back on, but almost nobody does."

items.q: What measurable effect did Emily report across a few hundred people?
options: After-hours pings fell by about a third
Notifications were switched back on by most staff
items.why: "the after-hours pings are down by a third, and focus blocks are actually being protected."

items.q: What does Emily mean by "we simply changed what happens if you do nothing"?
options: The default outcome now favours the desired behaviour
Nothing actually changed for most employees
The change only affects people who ignore their inbox
Employees were required to opt in to the new settings
items.why: Inferência: como a maioria não mexe nas configurações, mudar o default já muda o comportamento sem esforço.

items.q: Why does Emily say "nobody is celebrating it" is actually the point?
options: The results were disappointing and not worth marking
Celebrations would encourage people to undo the settings
The team was told not to publicise the change
A well-designed environment works so quietly that it goes unnoticed
items.why: Inferência: o sucesso do design é justamente ser invisível — o ambiente faz o trabalho que antes se pedia à força de vontade.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Every company-wide tool rollout reshapes how people work." A rollout is…
options: a report on how a tool is being used
a phased retirement of a legacy system
a routine software update installed automatically
the introduction or deployment of something across an organisation
items.why: Rollout = implantação: colocar algo em uso por toda a empresa.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We ___ meetings at fifty minutes so everyone gets ten minutes back."
items.why: To cap = limitar a um teto — aqui, o teto de cinquenta minutos por reunião.

items.q: "Leading at scale means managing the shape of attention, not just individual habits." This phrase refers to…
options: how the whole organisation's focus is collectively distributed
the physical layout of the open-plan office
the visual design of the company's software
the attention span of a single employee
items.why: Shape of attention = a forma como a atenção coletiva da empresa é distribuída.

items.q: "These settings were never revisited after installation." To revisit here means to…
items.why: To revisit = revisitar, voltar a examinar e reconsiderar uma decisão.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Making the right behaviour the easy one is a ___, not a matter of ___."
items.why: A tese da lição: é um problema de design (do ambiente), não de força de vontade (willpower).

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em decisões sobre produtividade e ferramentas. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The COO still has to sign off on the new default settings before Monday." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the capped-meeting policy region by region." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, aos poucos.

items.q: "A few managers pushed back on switching notifications off." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "They agreed to protect focus blocks but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it out to the end
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "A one-off webinar won't move the needle on after-hours work." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir diferença perceptível nos resultados.
